case.title: Adform supply-chain crypto clipper
case.boundary: The evidence supports malicious code presence, replacement capability, pre-incident activity at both replacement wallets and a separate ETH-to-BTC routing path. Overlapping BTC and ETH activity is consistent with, but does not prove, one shared collection episode. It does not establish which payments came from Adform visitors, completed theft, operator identity, or knowing participation by observed services and page owners.

nodes.label: Captured JavaScript
nodes.meaning: A public gist preserved the supplied malicious JavaScript and served as the seed artefact.

nodes.label: Adform script path
nodes.meaning: The investigation associated the payload with the trackpoint-async.js delivery path. Archived responses preserve time-bounded variants.

nodes.label: Four exact response hashes
nodes.meaning: Four distinct SHA-256 response values were grouped from passive observations and archived material. Exact hashes prevent similarity from being treated as identity.

nodes.label: 83 passive observations
nodes.meaning: The released CSV contains time-bounded urlscan observations. These rows are not proof of compromise, operator control or loss.

nodes.label: 59 unique page hostnames
nodes.meaning: Deduplicating page_hostname across the released rows produces 59 unique hostnames. This is a reproducible transformation, not a victim count.

nodes.label: Wallet replacement capability
nodes.meaning: Recovered response variants contained valid BTC and ETH replacement logic. Code capability does not prove that a transfer occurred.

nodes.label: Operator and loss not established
nodes.meaning: The released evidence does not prove a completed replacement, transferred funds, operator identity or knowing participation by observed site owners.

nodes.label: Wallets active before Adform
nodes.meaning: Both functioning replacement wallets collected and forwarded value before the reported incident window. Their overlapping 18 July activity is consistent with, but does not prove, one shared collection episode.

nodes.label: Seven calls name one BTC destination
nodes.meaning: Relays funded from the ETH replacement wallet routed 23.15 ETH, 15,258 USDT and 33,590 USDC through Harbor and Bridgers calls whose decoded destination is one Bitcoin address. That destination differs from the embedded BTC replacement wallet.

nodes.label: Routing service is not identity
nodes.meaning: Harbor and Bridgers are identified routing services, not identified mixers or operators. Exchange hot-wallet labels identify immediate senders, not customers.
